These applications have been filed seeking review of the judgment dated 27.07.2018 and seeking condonation of delay in filing the same.
2. The learned counsel for the appellants/applicants submits that this Court has erred in not awarding compensation towards loss of consortium in favour of the appellants/applicants.
3. I find merit in the above submission.

4. The Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi and Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680,
as explained by United India Insurance Company Ltd. v. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and Ors.,
(2021) 11 SCC 780, has held that in case of the death of a person in a motor accident, the family members/claimants shall be entitled the parental, filial, and spousal consortium, all at the rate of Rs.40,000/- for each of the Claimants.

Clearly, there is an error apparent on the face of the record in the judgment dated 27.07.2018 inasmuch, it failed to award loss of consortium in favour of the claimants.

As the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 is a beneficiary legislation which is aimed at granting relief to the victims of a motor accident,
instead of taking a technical view on the delay in filing the appeals, I deem it appropriate to condone the same.

6. Accordingly, the claimants are held entitled to loss of consortium in terms of the judgments referred hereinabove, and the Impugned Award is modified and it is directed that the claimants/appellants shall be entitled to loss of consortium at the rate of Rs.40,000/- for each of the Claimants.

7. The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate awarded by the learned Tribunal, that is 9%
per annum, till the passing of the judgment dated 27.07.2018, and thereafter from the date of filing of the present review petitions till the deposit of the enhanced amount by the Insurance Company with the learned Tribunal.
The enhanced amount of compensation along with interest thereon, shall be deposited by the Insurance Company with the learned Tribunal within a period of six weeks from today.
8. The claimants are also seeking grant of compensation towards loss of love and affection.

They place reliance on the judgment dated 25.07.2019 passed by this Court in a batch of appeals,
including MAC.APPL.785/2018, titled Lal Chand v. Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd and Anr.

sentences.text: It is contended that the appellants in these batch of appeals were co-passengers who had lost their lives in the same accident.

It is stated that in those appeals, the learned Tribunal had awarded compensation towards loss of love and affection in favour of the claimants therein and the same was not interfered with by this Court.

The learned counsel for the appellants/applicants submits that similar relief be extended to the present appellants/applicants as well.
10. I do not find any merit in the above claim of the appellants/applicants.

11. The Supreme Court in its judgment of Pranay Sethi (supra) has explained that in case of death in a motor accident, the only conventional heads of compensation are the loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses.
It is for this reason, this Court vide its judgment dated 27.07.2018 stated that the claimants were not entitled to any compensation towards loss of love and affection.

Merely because this issue had escaped the attention of this Court in the subsequent Ishwar Singh And Anr vs Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd ... on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160465430/
2 judgment dated 25.07.2019, would not entitle the appellants/applicants to seek the same relief in the present appeals, as it will be in teeth of the judgment of the Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (supra).
12.

accordingly, rejected.
13. The applications are disposed of in the above terms.
